The story presents distinct, believable perspectives: Miriam’s compromised leadership, Noor’s precarious working conditions, the lecturers’ frustrated adaptations, and Danny’s limited control over the work. Less sympathetic institutional figures are convincing through their evasive language and procedural responses rather than portrayed as simple villains. Miriam’s own failures—her unanswered appeal and refusal to discuss the hot-desk rota—also give her moral complexity without undermining her sympathetic portrayal.
